## ...inferring causality

**Example**

We are investigating the relationship between dressing in formal wear, wealth, and job offers. 

We recruit three people, *Person 1*, *Person 2*, and *Person 3*. *Person 1* and *Person 2* are married to each other. *Person 1* and *Person 3* are newly acquainted colleagues. 

# Classic causal inference

## Assumptions

### 0. No assumptions

```{r }
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-align: center
#| label: fig-fullly-connected-dag
#| fig-cap: "Fully connected causal DAG"

make_dag("fully_connected")         |> 
  plot_swig(node_radius = 0.2) + 
  scale_fill_mpxnyc(option = "light") +

```

### 3. Identical distribution

```{r}
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 6.5

make_dag("independence") |>

```

$$
\begin{aligned}
L_i &= f_{L}( U_{L_i}) \\
A_i &= f_{A}( U_{A_i}, L_i) \\
Y_i &= f_{Y}( U_{Y_i}, L_i, A_i) \\

$$ {#eq-independence-dag}

# Network causal inference

## Assumptions

### 0. No assumptions

```{r }
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-align: center
#| label: fig-fullly-connected-dag-2
#| fig-cap: "Fully connected causal DAG"

make_dag("fully_connected")         |> 
  plot_swig(node_radius = 0.2) + 
  scale_fill_mpxnyc(option = "light") +
  theme_mpxnyc_blank()

```

## Assumptions

### 1. No spillover

```{r}
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-align: center
#| label: fig-no-spillover-dag-2
#| fig-cap: "Causal DAG with no spillover"


make_dag("full_interference")      |> 
  plot_swig(node_radius = 0.2) + 
  scale_fill_mpxnyc(labels = c("h"), option = "light") +
  theme_mpxnyc_blank()


```

## Assumptions

### 2. Homogenous network interference

```{r}
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-align: center
#| label: fig-interference-dag
#| fig-cap: "Causal DAG with network interference"

make_dag("network_interference")   |> 
  plot_swig(node_radius = 0.2) + 
  scale_fill_mpxnyc(option = "light") +
  theme_mpxnyc_blank()


```


## 2. Homogenous network interference

### a. Loyalty

$$
\begin{aligned}
L_1 &= f_{L_1}(U_{L_1}) \\
L_2 &= f_{L_2}(U_{L_2}) \\
L_3 &= f_{L_3}(U_{L_3} ) \\
A_1 &= f_{A_1}(U_{A_1}, L_1, L_2) \\
A_2 &= f_{A_2}(U_{A_2}, L_1, L_2) \\
A_3 &= f_{A_3}(U_{A_3}, L_3) \\
Y_1 &= f_{Y_1}(U_{Y_1}, L_1, L_2, A_1, A_2) \\
Y_2 &= f_{Y_2}(U_{Y_2}, L_1, L_2, A_1, A_2) \\
Y_3 &= f_{Y_3}(U_{Y_3}, L_3,  A_3) \\
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-interference-dag}


## 2. Homogenous network interference
### b. Separability

$$
\begin{aligned}
L_1 &= f_{L_1}(U_{L_1}) \\
L_2 &= f_{L_2}(U_{L_2}) \\
L_3 &= f_{L_3}(U_{L_3} ) \\
A_1 &= f_{A_1}(U_{A_1}, L_1, g_{A_1}(\mathbf{L}, 1)) \\
A_2 &= f_{A_2}(U_{A_2}, L_2, g_{A_2}(\mathbf{L}, 2)) \\
A_3 &= f_{A_3}(U_{A_3}, L_3, g_{A_3}(\mathbf{L}, 3)) \\
Y_1 &= f_{Y_1}(U_{Y_1}, L_1, A_1, g_{Y_1}(\mathbf{L}, 1), h_{Y_1}(\mathbf{A}, 1)) \\
Y_2 &= f_{Y_2}(U_{Y_2}, L_2, A_2, g_{Y_2}(\mathbf{L}, 2), h_{Y_2}(\mathbf{A}, 2)) \\
Y_3 &= f_{Y_3}(U_{Y_3}, L_3,A_3,  g_{Y_2}(\mathbf{L}, 3), h_{Y_2}(\mathbf{A}, 3)) \\
\end{aligned}
$$

## 2. Homogenous network interference

### c. Positional invariance

$$
\begin{aligned}
L_1 &= f_{L_1}(U_{L_1}) \\
L_2 &= f_{L_2}(U_{L_2}) \\
L_3 &= f_{L_3}(U_{L_3} ) \\
A_1 &= f_{A_1}(U_{A_1}, L_1, g_{A}(\mathbf{L}, 1)) \\
A_2 &= f_{A_2}(U_{A_2}, L_2, g_{A}(\mathbf{L}, 2)) \\
A_3 &= f_{A_3}(U_{A_3}, L_3, g_{A}(\mathbf{L}, 3)) \\
Y_1 &= f_{Y_1}(U_{Y_1}, L_1, A_1, g_{Y}(\mathbf{L}, 1), h_{Y}(\mathbf{A}, 1)) \\
Y_2 &= f_{Y_2}(U_{Y_2}, L_2, A_2, g_{Y}(\mathbf{L}, 2), h_{Y}(\mathbf{A}, 2)) \\
Y_3 &= f_{Y_3}(U_{Y_3}, L_3,A_3,  g_{Y}(\mathbf{L}, 3), h_{Y}(\mathbf{A}, 3)) \\
\end{aligned}
$$

## 2. Homogenous network interference

### d. Symmetry

For permutation matrix $\mathbf{M} \in \{0,1\}^{n\times n}$, $\mathbf{X}, \mathbf{X}' \in \{0,1\}^n$, alter set $\mathscr{N}_i$ (indices of nodes connected to $i$)

$$
\begin{equation}
\mathbf{X}_{\mathscr{N}_i} = \mathbf{M} \mathbf{X'}_{\mathscr{N}_i}  \\
\implies \\
g_{ti}(\mathbf{X}, i) = g_{ti}(\mathbf{X'}, i) 
\end{equation}
$$

where $\mathbf{X}_{\mathscr{N}_i}$ is the subvector of $\mathbf{X}$ containing entries related to indices contained by $\mathscr{N}_i$.



## 2. Homogenous network interference

### e. Boundedness

We say that an exposure mapping $g_{i}$ is bounded if all possible exposure values are contained by a finite set $\mathbf{D}$


## 3. Identical distribution

```{r}
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-align: center
#| label: fig-homogenous-dag
#| fig-cap: "Causal DAG with homogenous structure"


make_dag("homogenous_interference")            |> 
  plot_swig(node_radius = 0.2) + 
  scale_fill_mpxnyc(option = "light") +
  theme_mpxnyc_blank()


```

$$
\begin{aligned}
L_i &= f_{L}( U_{L_i} ) \\
A_i &= f_{A}( U_{A_i}, L_i, g_{A}(\textbf{L}, i) ) \\
Y_i &= f_{Y}( U_{Y_i},  L_i,  g_{Y}(\textbf{L}, i),   A_i,  h_{Y}( \textbf{A}, i ) ) \\
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-homogenous-dag}

## Compact structure

### Directed Acyclic Network Graph (DANG)

```{r}
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-width: 5
#| label: fig-causal-dang-instructions
#| fig-cap: Causal DANG

structural <- example_dang_1_structural() |>
                    plot_swig(node_radius = 0.2) +
                    scale_fill_mpxnyc(option = "light") +
                    theme_mpxnyc_blank()+
                    ggplot2::ggtitle("Structural Part") 

relational <- example_dang_1_relational() |>
                    plot_swig(0, 0, node_radius = 0.2)  +
                    scale_fill_mpxnyc(name = "Entity type", option = "light") +
                    theme_mpxnyc_blank() +
                    ggplot2::ggtitle("Relational Part") 

cowplot::plot_grid(structural, relational, ncol = 1)

```

## Flexible structure

### DANG

```{r}
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-align: center
#| label: fig-example-dang-structural
#| fig-cap: "Causal DANG for Week 1 in Example 3"


structural  <- example_dang_2_structural() |>
                    plot_swig(node_radius = 0.15) +
                    scale_fill_mpxnyc(option = "light") +
                    theme_mpxnyc_blank() +
                    ggplot2::ggtitle("Structural Part")


relational  <- example_dang_2_relational() |>
                    plot_swig(node_radius = 0.2, node_margin = 0)  +
                    scale_fill_mpxnyc(name = "Entity type", option = "light") +
                    theme_mpxnyc_blank() +
                    ggplot2::ggtitle("Relational Part") 

figure   <- cowplot::plot_grid(structural, relational, ncol=1, rel_heights = c(3,3))



legend_pre  <- relational + ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "right")

legend      <- cowplot::get_legend(legend_pre) 
 
   
cowplot::plot_grid(figure, legend, nrow = 1, rel_widths = c(4,1))
```

## Flexible structure

### Single World Intervention Network Graph (SWING)

```{r}
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-align: center
#| label: fig-example-swig-structural
#| fig-cap: "SWING for Week 1 in Example 3"
#| 


structural  <- example_swing_structural() |>
                    plot_swig(node_radius = 0.15) +
                    scale_fill_mpxnyc(option = "light") +
                    theme_mpxnyc_blank() +
                    ggplot2::ggtitle("Structural Part") 


relational  <- example_swing_relational() |>
                    plot_swig(node_radius = 0.2, node_margin = 0)  +
                    scale_fill_mpxnyc(name = "Entity type", option = "light") +
                    ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "right") +
                    theme_mpxnyc_blank() +
                    ggplot2::ggtitle("Relational Part")


legend_pre  <- relational +
                    ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "right")
legend      <- cowplot::get_legend(legend_pre) 



figure   <- cowplot::plot_grid(structural, relational, ncol=1, rel_heights = c(3,3))

cowplot::plot_grid(figure, legend, nrow = 1, rel_widths = c(4,1))

```

## Structural equations
$$
\begin{aligned}
M_{0i} &=  0 \\
V_{0i} &=  0 \\
R_{sj}^{(h)} &=  h(\mathbf{V}_{s-1}) \\
T_{sj}^{(h)} &=  \begin{cases} 1 & R_{sj}^{(h)} = max_k R_{sk}^{(h)} \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \\
M_{si}^{(h)} &=  \begin{cases} 1 & \mathbf{T}_{s\mathscr{N}_i}^{(h)} \neq \mathbf{0}  \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \\
V_{si}^{(h)} &=  \begin{cases} 1 & M_{si}^{(h)} = 1 \text{ or } V_{s-1,i}^{(h)} = 1\\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \\
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-edge-intervention-swing}
